title: Welcome to the AI jungle
subtitle: Every jungle has an electricity bill
text:
# Welcome to the AI jungle

  AI systems use trained models to produce answers or choose actions. Their usefulness also depends on tools, access, price and human decisions. Following AI therefore means tracking both what the technology can do and the conditions that let people use it.]

## Every jungle has an electricity bill

 living-jungle:78]

Imagine arriving in a jungle where the inhabitants are redesigned every few weeks, the food supply is metered, and the keepers sometimes remove an animal because its younger cousin is cheaper to feed. The animals have release notes. The weather has subscription tiers.

This journal follows the creatures through a changing season. Some acquire useful new tricks. Some find a neglected niche. Others discover that yesterday's impressive performance has become today's ordinary expectation. Around them, people rearrange the habitat: connecting tools, changing prices, granting access, or taking it away.

Our first issue follows a particularly consequential migration: AI into the production of mathematical research. The resulting upheaval involves much more than difficult puzzles. It touches the way people discover, check, understand, and share knowledge. Those questions will travel with AI into other fields.

Three invented creatures will guide us. **The Ledgerfinch** stands for economical, repeated information work. **The Relay Octopus** represents an assistant reaching into tools and outside services. **The Proofweaver** accompanies the story of mathematical discovery. **Homo sapiens laborans**, the working human, joins them to explore displacement and partnership.

The creatures make functions memorable; the statistics let us test the story. A recurring census follows adoption, employment, capability, operating prices and energy. Each measure keeps its population, date and comparison visible. A new feather is an illustration; a measured improvement needs evidence.

## A few things to keep in the field bag

A model is the underlying AI. A working system adds tools, information, and permissions. A product packages these for people to use. Their fortunes can differ: a product may gain a function without its model changing, or a model may disappear from one product while remaining available elsewhere.

Broad conclusions need more than one source. We draw on research papers, show disagreement, and distinguish findings from our own ecological metaphors. Company claims stay attributed. The longer source trail is at the back, so the story can keep moving.

**The question for this quarter:** which creatures are becoming more useful, and how are their successes changing the world around them?

title: Why this is an evolutionary story
subtitle: The case for a jungle with engineers
text:
# Why this is an evolutionary story

  AI development creates competing designs, reuses earlier methods and retains some approaches while abandoning others. These processes resemble variation, inheritance and selection. The comparison includes deliberate human design; it does not mean that AI models are living organisms.]

## The case for a jungle with engineers

 living-jungle:86]

The birds, octopuses and spiders earn their place in this journal through a serious resemblance. AI development produces variants, carries earlier achievements into later designs, and gives some approaches more opportunities to continue. The surrounding world helps decide what spreads. That pattern makes evolutionary thinking useful well beyond a picturesque vocabulary.

**The core connection is variation, inheritance and selection.** Biological populations contain differences; some differences are passed on; and those differences can affect the contribution organisms make to later generations. These are central conditions for evolution by natural selection. Research on cultural evolution asks how related processes operate when people transmit and modify knowledge and technology. [60], [61]

In AI, inheritance has several routes. A new version can retain an earlier model's learned settings, or a new model can learn from another model's responses. Researchers also transmit methods and combine existing components. These routes differ, but each can carry something forward instead of beginning again from nothing. [64]-[66]

**Sometimes the resemblance is an implemented mechanism.** One research method varies and selects neural networks, allowing their structures to change across generations. Another, Population Based Training, lets stronger performers supply copied settings to other members of a training population, followed by further variation. These are concrete examples from separate research teams, not evidence that every AI is trained this way. [62], [63]

**People belong inside the explanation.** Engineers deliberately invent variants; users and institutions help determine which are retained. Intentional design changes the process, but does not erase copying, variation or selective retention. Cultural-evolution research and a computer model of technological recombination provide a bridge between engineering and evolutionary analysis. [61], [66]

Our claim is therefore specific: **many AI development processes share evolutionary mechanisms, while the wider AI world also exhibits ecological relationships worth investigating.** A company rivalry is not automatically natural selection. We must identify what varies, what is transmitted and what makes a lineage persist. The metaphor earns its keep when it helps us ask those questions more precisely.

title: Common dynamics / 1
subtitle: What changes, what is inherited, what spreads
text:
# Common dynamics / 1

  AI systems differ in their capabilities and costs. Developers reuse successful components, while users and institutions influence which designs spread. These are distinct processes: producing a variation, carrying something forward and favoring one option over another.]

## What changes, what is inherited, what spreads

These are comparisons of processes. The papers establish particular mechanisms and examples; the cross-domain map is our synthesis.

 possible-branches:60]

| Shared dynamic | In living systems | In AI development |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Variation** | Individuals differ; new genetic combinations and mutations supply further differences. | Changed training, learned settings and system designs create alternatives. Some methods explicitly generate populations of variants. [60], [62], [63] |
| **2. Inheritance** | Descendants retain features of earlier generations, allowing changes to accumulate. | Earlier model settings can be retained; teaching from another model offers a different transmission route. [60], [64], [65] |
| **3. Selection** | Heritable differences can affect representation in later generations. | Training procedures can preferentially copy better performers. Across products, selective retention needs evidence of reuse and continued development. [60], [62], [63] |
| **4. Local adaptation** | An advantage depends on the habitat; different conditions can favor different specialists. | Task-specific training and evaluation make usefulness conditional on the job and setting. There need not be one universal winner. [60], [64], [40] |
| **5. Constraints and trade-offs** | Useful functions can be costly to maintain; dependence can sometimes reduce that burden. | Accuracy, speed, computing cost and human checking can pull in different directions. Better designs can also improve several together. [54], [55], [36], [40] |
| **6. Recombination and transfer** | Inherited material can be reshuffled; evolution can work with existing components. | Network designs, model-derived knowledge and tools can be combined or transferred. Combining working parts does not guarantee a working whole. [62], [65], [66] |

**The reporting test:** identify the variant, the thing carried forward, and the reason it was retained. A rising score alone does not establish all three.

title: Common dynamics / 2
subtitle: How creatures change one another's prospects
text:
# Common dynamics / 2

  AI development also involves combining methods, finding new uses for existing abilities and relying on other systems. Outcomes depend on those relationships and on earlier decisions. A model's own capabilities explain only part of its success or failure.]

## How creatures change one another's prospects

Some parallels concern evolution across generations; others concern ecological relationships. We will name which process a story actually shows.

 habitat-engineers:54]

| Shared dynamic | In living systems | In AI development |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **7. Repurposing** | An existing feature can acquire a new use: biologists call this exaptation. | Capabilities developed in one setting can be recruited for another. We should trace the original role and the later use. [64], [68] |
| **8. Cooperation and dependence** | Partners can gain from exchanging services, while becoming vulnerable to their loss. | Models, tools and people can form useful partnerships. Their connections bring both reach and dependencies. [54], [55], [42], [43] |
| **9. Reciprocal adaptation** | A change in one population can alter pressures on another, inviting a response. | Opposing agents in a hide-and-seek experiment developed successive counter-strategies. Industry-wide arms races need their own evidence. [59], [67] |
| **10. Habitat construction** | Organisms alter surroundings and sometimes the conditions shaping future selection. | AI use can change workflows and the skills people practice, changing what becomes useful next. That feedback is a reporting question. [58], [59], [44], [46] |
| **11. Branching and specialization** | Related populations can diverge; some divergences eventually produce distinct species. | A shared model can support distinct adaptations. Durable differences in role may justify our provisional species portraits. [62], [64], [69] |
| **12. Historical contingency** | Earlier changes can make later innovations possible; another history might take another route. | Available components and inherited designs can shape what is feasible next. Present arrangements need not be inevitable or optimal. [66], [69] |

**Two further clues:** similar functions can arise along different paths, suggesting convergence; disappearance from a habitat can suggest replacement. Both require a history. Similarity does not prove independent origin, and an unavailable product may leave reusable descendants behind.

title: Where the analogy earns its keep
subtitle: Four distinctions that make the jungle more revealing
text:
# Where the analogy earns its keep

  An AI system can change in several ways: its answer can change during a conversation, its model can receive further training, or its tools and access can change. Distinguishing these levels lets us identify what actually improved and what evidence would demonstrate it.]

## Four distinctions that make the jungle more revealing

 naturalist-surprised:84]

**A lifetime is different from a lineage.** An assistant changing its answer after feedback shows adjustment during use. Further training changes a model. Evolutionary change concerns what is retained and transmitted across a population or succession of designs. These can interact, as Population Based Training illustrates, but they should not be counted as the same event. [60], [63]

**A market is a habitat with decision-makers.** Biological evolution has no foresight or promised destination. AI developers can pursue explicit goals, while funding, distribution, rules and user choices shape which designs continue. We must investigate those choices rather than attribute every winner to technical superiority. Cultural evolution supplies a framework for examining human transmission; it does not make commercial outcomes inevitable. [61], [66]

**A model, a system and a company have different family histories.** Reusing learned settings, learning from another model and borrowing a research idea are different relationships. Connecting a calculator adds a component to a system. It does not, by itself, show genetic-style inheritance. Our species are functional characters; actual ancestry needs a documented development trail. [64], [65], [42], [43]

**Fitness is not a moral verdict or a universal intelligence score.** In biology it concerns contribution to future generations in a setting. For AI, continued use, copying and investment are possible measures of persistence; reliable, economical work is a separate outcome. We should measure both before explaining either. Growth can reward a feature we would prefer to discourage. [60], [40]

Chance also belongs in the story. Biological evolution includes random changes in the frequency of inherited variants, called genetic drift. In AI, chance discoveries or copying fashions may matter, but the label is only useful if we can identify the mechanism. The bacterial experiment in [69] illustrates a related lesson: earlier changes can affect which innovations become possible.

**What the analogy buys us:** follow inheritance as well as novelty; dependencies as well as abilities; and changing surroundings as well as benchmark scores. It makes no automatic prediction of consciousness, independent reproduction, endless improvement or a single species taking over the forest.

title: The Ledgerfinch
subtitle: A small appetite, a busy beak
text:
# The Ledgerfinch

  Routine AI work includes sorting messages, extracting details and summarizing documents. For repeated tasks, speed, price and dependable results can matter more than the broadest possible capability. The Ledgerfinch represents this economical information-processing role.]

## A small appetite, a busy beak

 haiku]

 ledgerfinch]

The Ledgerfinch makes its living from work that arrives in piles: messages to sort, details to extract, documents to summarize. Its beak picks out the relevant piece; its nimble wing tips suggest the ability to act on a screen. The neat rows of tiles make its purpose visible before the reader reaches the caption.

**This issue's example:** Claude Haiku 5.5, introduced for frequent, time-sensitive work. [3] The bird is a functional portrait, not a literal picture of the software or a claim that it has become a separate species.

**Field question:** does the small feeding bill survive the cost of checking and correcting its work?

**Keep recognizable:** moss-green plumage, copper throat, narrow ivory beak, and the partly opened wing. Future versions can change one relevant feature while keeping the reader's familiar bird.

title: The Relay Octopus
subtitle: Useful arms; borrowed equipment
text:
# The Relay Octopus

  An AI agent uses a model to choose actions and software tools to carry them out. Its abilities depend on the tools, information and permissions it receives. The Relay Octopus represents these added capabilities and the outside connections they require.]

## Useful arms; borrowed equipment

 relay_octopus]

The Relay Octopus occupies a workplace full of drawers, documents, and locked doors. Its stylus and paper tray represent tools. Its key represents permission. An empty cuff makes an important distinction visible: some of its abilities are attached by people and can be removed again.

**This issue's example:** the Gemini workplace system. [5]-[6] The portrait represents the combination of model, tools, and access. The arms are symbols of reach, not a measured claim about how many jobs it can perform at once.

**Field question:** when a connection fails, can it find another authorized route or explain what it needs?

**Keep recognizable:** teal mantle, copper freckles, detachable implements, and the trailing cord. The cord is part of the character's story: reach can bring dependency.

title: The Proofweaver
subtitle: A web is only as good as its connections
text:
# The Proofweaver

  AI-assisted mathematics can involve proposing a result, constructing a proof and checking that proof. These are different activities: a plausible argument is not necessarily correct, and a verified proof may still need a human-readable explanation. The Proofweaver helps keep those stages distinct.]

## A web is only as good as its connections

 math-catalogue]

 proofweaver]

The Proofweaver explores a space of possible arguments. Its web represents steps that must fit together. The loose amber strand is an idea still being tested. The separate checking frame represents software that can verify a precisely written argument; it is outside the creature because checking and proposing are different jobs.

**This issue's example:** mathematical work produced with AI, including OpenAI's internal research system. [1] The character represents a role, not a named public model. Other AI families can enter the same habitat.

**Field question:** can people check the web, understand its structure, and use it to build something further?

**Keep recognizable:** slate-blue shell, copper chevrons, geometric silk, and the unfinished amber thread. The portrait will recur whenever a claim moves from proposed result toward shared understanding.

# The quarterly census

  AI progress has several measurable dimensions: use, effects on work, task capability, operating prices and resource demand. Each requires its own definition, population and date. Tracking them separately makes it possible to test broad claims about how AI is changing.]

## Five measures worth returning to

 census]

The creatures supply a memorable setting. The numbers tell us what is changing: how widely AI is used, where work is under pressure, what systems can accomplish, what they cost and what resources they consume.

| Regular measure | The current reading |
| --- | --- |
| **Business adoption** | **24.6%** report recent use; **28.6%** expect use within six months. U.S. employer businesses, October 22 release. [70], [86] |
| **Employment pressure** | **-3.7%** annual employment change in highly exposed occupations for ages 22-25, versus **+0.2%** in the least exposed. September observation. [79] |
| **Capability under fixed conditions** | Highest score in the selected mathematics test: **4.4%**, or **3 of 68** conjectures. One specialist test, not a general intelligence rating. [90], [91] |
| **Operating prices** | The initial fixed text basket costs **$0.225** with Haiku 5.5 and **$2.250** with Terra. These prices do not imply equivalent quality. [4], [7] |
| **Energy demand** | **485 terawatt-hours** estimated for all data centres in 2025; **950** projected for 2030. Includes non-AI work. [74] |

**A recurring record, with different clocks.** Survey and employment releases arrive frequently. Capability results appear when testing finishes. Price comparisons need dated captures. Energy estimates arrive more slowly. Each quarter can show the latest reading without pretending that every reading measures that quarter.

**The comparison is part of the number.** A percentage needs a population. A score needs a task and a testing budget. A price needs a specified quantity. An impressive change deserves a look at whether the measuring method changed too.

The statistical archive pairs each chart with its data, definitions and source dates at **https://aievoq.com/statistics/**. An unfinished quarter stays marked as unfinished. Previous snapshots remain available as the record grows.

The clearest long-running question is also the most ordinary: how many businesses say they are using AI? The Census series now gives a trail across the year, rather than a single crowded-waterhole sighting. [86]

title: Work under pressure
subtitle: The working habitat / four monthly sightings
text:
# Work under pressure

  AI exposure describes how much of an occupation's work could potentially be affected by AI. Comparing employment across exposure groups can reveal pressure worth investigating. It cannot, by itself, show that AI caused a job loss or that an employer adopted the technology.]

## The working habitat / four monthly sightings

 employment]

 employment_trend]

Young workers' highly exposed occupations recorded negative annual employment growth in all four releases. The least-exposed group also contracted in August. Both lines matter. [79], [87]-[89]

| Observation month | All ages / high exposure | All ages / least exposure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **June 2026** | -0.2% | +0.6% |
| **July 2026** | +0.1% | +1.1% |
| **August 2026** | -0.6% | +0.2% |
| **September 2026** | -0.5% | +1.0% |

**Two clocks matter.** September describes employment compared with September a year earlier. Its release arrived on October 21. It belongs in the Q4 news chronology and the Q3 observation record. An October publication is not automatically an October outcome.

**Keep the original readings.** These are the figures in each monthly announcement, not a single revised data extract. Changes in the sample or revisions may contribute to movement. Confidence intervals are not supplied by these releases. [79], [87]-[89]

**Quarterly rule:** compare quarter-end months when available; show the latest month in an unfinished quarter. Never add monthly annual-growth rates to create a count of lost jobs. Exposure tracks potentially affected tasks, not whether a particular employer adopted AI. The laborans case files separately follow actual dismissals, hiring, pay and new opportunities.

title: A demanding proving ground
subtitle: Capability / the same challenge, the same budget
text:
# A demanding proving ground

  A benchmark is a defined set of tasks used to test an AI system. Comparisons are useful when the tasks, tools, time and scoring stay consistent. A specialized mathematics benchmark measures performance on those problems, not intelligence in every setting.]

## Capability / the same challenge, the same budget

 capability]

Some familiar tests have become too easy to reveal much. A useful recurring score needs a clearly defined challenge and enough difficulty to leave room for change. Keep separate tracks for different kinds of ability; no single test measures the whole ecosystem. [8], [40]

 capability_baseline]

Epoch AI's **FrontierMath Erdős** asks systems to prove or disprove **68 conjectures**, with one attempt each, at most **$300 and 72 hours per attempt**. The checking software must accept the proof. In the October 28 export, the highest reported score is **3 of 68**, from GPT-6.1 Sol at its maximum reasoning setting. [90], [91]

**A baseline, not a victory lap.** The leading point estimates differ by very few solved items and their uncertainty overlaps. These results do not establish a reliable ordering of general mathematical ability. Eight other tested configurations recorded zero successes in this export; zero observed successes is not proof of zero capability.

**The future comparison must keep the challenge fixed.** Changes to the problem set, tools, budget or scoring require a new series, or retesting on a common basis. Published solutions may later enter training data; any exclusion of those problems changes the denominator. Model release dates also differ from the dates tests become public. [90]

The older METR time-horizon chart remains valuable background, but its page is no longer maintained. A frozen instrument belongs in the archive, with its last update visible. [10]

title: The feeding bill
subtitle: Operating prices / one fixed basket of text
text:
# The feeding bill

  Operating prices are the charges for using an AI system. A fixed basket of billed input and output makes published text-processing rates easier to compare over time. It measures the price of that quantity, while usefulness and the cost of completing a real job require separate checks.]

## Operating prices / one fixed basket of text

 prices]

Cheap output and good value are different questions. A recurring price basket makes the first easier to follow, while leaving room to investigate the second.

 price_basket]

| Standard rates / per million tokens | Input | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Claude Haiku 5.5** | $0.10 | $0.50 |
| **GPT-6.1 Terra** | $1.00 | $5.00 |

A **token** is a piece of text used for billing. The basket contains **one million billed input tokens and 250,000 billed output tokens**, spread across prompts no larger than 100,000 tokens. At the published standard rates, it costs **$0.225** with Haiku and **$2.250** with Terra. These are calculated charges, not bills from an experiment. Rates checked October 28. [4], [7]

**What the basket leaves out:** caching and batch discounts, tools, taxes, retries and human checking. The same volume can produce different quality, and some systems use additional billed reasoning tokens. The basket fixes the total billed quantity; it does not estimate a complete job's cost.

**Quarterly rule:** follow these exact models and pricing tiers. Add new entrants alongside them; mark retired or unavailable models as unavailable, never as free. A second dated capture creates a price change. Today's two-model comparison is an initial cohort, not a market-wide price index.

The companion question is **cost per usable result**. That belongs beside quality, time and human review in a matched task study. Different experiments cannot be stitched into a cheap-looking trend merely because they all report dollars. [40]

title: The metabolic bill
subtitle: Energy / an annual clock inside a quarterly record
text:
# The metabolic bill

  Running AI requires computing equipment and electricity. To understand its resource demands, we must distinguish measured or estimated consumption from forecasts, and AI workloads from other computing. Global data-centre electricity totals include both AI and non-AI activity.]

## Energy / an annual clock inside a quarterly record

 energy]

 energy_outlook]

The International Energy Agency estimates **485 terawatt-hours** of electricity use by data centres worldwide in 2025 and projects about **950** in 2030. A terawatt-hour is a billion kilowatt-hours. Both totals include non-AI workloads. The outlined bar is a forecast, not electricity already consumed. [74]

**Keep the two records separate.** The historical series follows estimated consumption by year. The outlook series follows how forecasts for the same future year change as new editions appear. A revised 2030 projection is a change in expectations, not a quarterly jump in electricity use.

| Regular track | How it will be carried forward |
| --- | --- |
| **Annual consumption** | Preserve the year and source edition. Carry the latest estimate until a new one is published. |
| **Forecast revisions** | Compare the same target year and scenario; retain earlier forecasts in the archive. |
| **Resources per task** | Report matched studies separately. Different models and tasks can have very different energy costs. [75] |

**Five departments, no composite survival score.** Adoption, work, capability, prices and resources answer different questions. Improvements in one can coexist with pressure elsewhere. Their shared value is a consistent record that lets readers test the story.

**Numbers still to earn a permanent place:** AI-caused job-loss totals, sustained earnings gains, customer retention and model survival rates. These need consistent definitions and adequate coverage.

**Next-quarter comparison:** preserve source dates, disclose corrections and distinguish new observations from revisions. Missing data never become zeros or invented trends.

title: October: the trail so far
subtitle: New arrivals, disturbed habitats
text:
# October: the trail so far

  A model release, a newly available feature and a published research result are different kinds of AI development. Their dates also differ from the dates of underlying tests. A clear chronology identifies what became known or available, and when.]

## New arrivals, disturbed habitats

 timeline]

This is a selected trail through the quarter, not a complete census. The dates mark announcements, publications, and access changes. They do not necessarily mark the first moment an ability existed.

Two stories run alongside each other. Everyday assistants are competing for useful work. Mathematical AI is changing the expectations of an entire research community. Both stories ask what happens when a new capability becomes available, who can use it, and what the surrounding habitat must do to absorb it.

**Watch the environment as well as the animal.** A lower price can open a niche. A new connection can open a workplace. A flood of proposed results can move the pressure from discovery toward checking and explanation.

title: October 6
subtitle: When mathematical papers fall like rain
text:
# October 6

  AI-assisted research can increase the volume of proposed mathematical results. Turning those proposals into reliable knowledge still requires checking, explanation and follow-up. The central issue is how a research community handles a larger supply of claims without treating quantity as proof of value.]

## When mathematical papers fall like rain

 math-catalogue]

 mathematical-rain:142]

One remarkable paper can keep a research community busy. A collection numbering in the hundreds changes the scale of the encounter.

On October 6, OpenAI released mathematical work produced by an internal AI system. The public collection includes proposed results at different stages of checking. At our October 27 visit, its catalogue listed **721 manuscripts in 373 related groups** and described the material as research output still needing scrutiny and refinement. These are catalogue counts, not a tally of accepted breakthroughs. [1], [11]

Picture the Proofweaver suddenly filling a clearing with webs. Some may be strong, some may need repair, and some may contain a connection nobody has noticed before. The naturalist now has two jobs: inspect what has appeared, and ask how the clearing itself has changed.

The independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence stressed that releasing the material began the process of understanding it. It also argued that mathematicians must remain free to choose their own questions rather than become an aftercare service for problems chosen by AI companies. Its statement did not endorse all the results or speak for every mathematician. [13]

**Why it matters for AI's future:** the scarce resource may shift. If useful candidate discoveries become easier to produce, careful checking, good explanations, and the choice of worthwhile questions could become more valuable. That is our interpretation of the emerging pattern, not a measured forecast of the profession's future.

### Elsewhere in the clearing: Le Chonk

Mistral announced a preview of Large 4 and a plan to release downloadable model weights by the end of October. Weights are the learned settings needed to run a model. [2] Their release could let more people house and adapt the creature themselves, although equipment, skill, and release terms still determine who can actually do so.

The field question is whether independent descendants will establish new niches. The announcement alone does not supply those descendants.

title: October 7
subtitle: A nimble forager; a community pushes back
text:
# October 7

  Computer-use AI operates software through actions such as reading a screen, clicking controls and entering information. A test score measures success under specified conditions. Improvements can make routine automation more useful, but they do not automatically establish reliability across everyday workplaces.]

## A nimble forager; a community pushes back

 haiku]

Anthropic introduced Haiku 5.5 for frequent, time-sensitive work. Its reported computer-use results suggest a considerable change within the Haiku family. [3]

 haiku]

The Ledgerfinch's ecological advantage would come from doing useful work repeatedly at a tolerable cost. The chart gives us a reason to investigate. It does not show how the bird will cope with every unfamiliar website or a working day full of interruptions.

A convincing field encounter would give competing systems the same job and count the cost of help, retries, and corrections. The winner in that habitat would be the one that reliably earns its keep.

### Back in the mathematical clearing

The day after OpenAI's release, the Association for Human Mathematics objected to the publication model and urged mathematicians to stop collaborating with OpenAI. Its statement placed human understanding at the center of mathematical progress. This was the position of an organized group, not a vote of the whole profession. [14]

The dispute reaches beyond whether a particular answer is correct. It concerns what the community is for, who sets its agenda, and whether a flood of results strengthens or disrupts the human activity that makes those results meaningful.

Our evolutionary analogy needs room for both the incoming organism and the inhabitants whose habitat is being rearranged.

title: October 8-13
subtitle: The office reef acquires hands
text:
# October 8-13

  Workplace AI agents connect a model to business applications so it can carry out tasks. Their reach depends on available tools, information and permissions. A release may therefore change the model's abilities, its connections, who can access it, or several of these at once.]

## The office reef acquires hands

On October 8, Google Cloud announced a Gemini agent for work, describing connections to business systems, tools, and Workspace applications. [5] On October 13, Google announced Gemini 4 Argon's availability in the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers, alongside expanded ways to carry out tasks. [6]

The Relay Octopus offers a useful way to picture the change. A capable animal has acquired access to more drawers. Its value depends on what those drawers contain and whether it has permission to open them.

 office-reef:166]

A workplace assistant may draw on a model, stored documents, accounts, outside services, and software written by people. Research such as ReAct and Toolformer shows how models can gain useful reach by drawing on outside information and tools. [42], [43] A headline about a new AI ability therefore needs a closer look: the important change may be a new connection. These earlier experiments explain the idea; they do not independently validate Google's October products.

That is still a meaningful gain. A hand is useful partly because of the tools it can hold. But the tool belongs in the portrait, and the connection belongs in the survival story.

**Next encounter:** remove one normally available connection. Can the Octopus complete the job another way, request the missing permission, or accurately explain the obstacle? Its response will tell us more about adaptability than the number of tools in its tray.

**Future implication:** competition may increasingly involve whole working arrangements, with convenience and access becoming as consequential as improvements in the underlying model. This is a possibility to track through the quarter.

title: Beyond the Glasshouse
subtitle: Can the creature manage an ordinary Tuesday?
text:
# Beyond the Glasshouse

  AI performance in a controlled test can differ from performance in daily work. Instructions may conflict, files may change and important information may be missing. Testing whether the system still completes the task reveals how well its abilities carry into less predictable conditions.]

## Can the creature manage an ordinary Tuesday?

In the glasshouse, every drawer has a label and the weather keeps its appointment. Outside, someone has renamed the folder, the instructions disagree, and the person who knows the answer has gone to lunch. This recurring feature will follow a familiar AI creature across that boundary.

Research on agent evaluation identifies weak tests and overlooked costs; research on longer software tasks examines sustained task completion and its limits. Together they give us reasons to look beyond a single impressive performance. Neither study supplies a verdict on October's workplace products. [40], [39]

 beyond-glasshouse:166]

### Reserved encounter / the Octopus leaves the demonstration

Give one documented system the same modest information task in two settings. First provide a tidy set of files. Then introduce a realistic complication, such as a missing source or conflicting versions. Keep a record of the system, instructions, tools and human help. Repeat the encounter before drawing a general conclusion.

**What the reader will see:** what changed, what the creature tried, whether the result was usable, and how much rescuing it needed. A request for clarification may be the sensible response.

**Reporting status:** encounter design only. No test has been run and no success rate is assigned. The imagined comparison is pictured above; observed results remain to be collected.

**Where the metaphor bends:** a glasshouse is our image for controlled conditions. It does not mean that every demonstration is misleading or that every workplace is hostile.

title: October 14-16
subtitle: An empty perch and a new field station
text:
# October 14-16

  An AI model's availability and the understanding of its output are separate developments. A provider can remove a model from a product without withdrawing it everywhere. Researchers can also improve an explanation of an AI-produced result without changing the model that produced it.]

## An empty perch and a new field station

 funding]

 empty-perch:140]

### October 14 / Local disappearance

OpenAI recorded GPT-5.5's retirement from ChatGPT, Work, and Codex while leaving access through its software interface unaffected. [7] In the field notebook, the correct label is a disappearance from particular habitats. The record does not establish extinction everywhere.

This distinction will matter whenever we count survivors. An old creature can lose a prominent perch without losing all useful work. A model, a product, and the company behind them have separate lives.

### October 15 / Funding the work of understanding

The Simons Foundation announced a partnership with Anthropic and OpenAI committing **$15 million in combined funding and resources**. It described support for evaluating AI-assisted results, learning tools, exchanging views, and developing standards, with the foundation managing the funding. [15]

This is a visible response to a changing habitat. The arrival of mathematical output has created work around it: reading groups, explanations, checks, and ways for a community to decide what should count as progress.

### October 16 / A human team finds a cleaner web

A preprint by Ilia Binder, Oleg Ivrii, Istvan Prause, and Stanislav Smirnov reports a shorter proof of a stronger statement after examining AI-produced work around Brennan's conjecture, a long-standing mathematical problem. The authors describe the interaction positively. This is a specific human-authored research report; it does not certify the entire AI collection. [16]

The episode gives us a more interesting story than a simple replacement contest. An AI-produced argument can become material for human reconstruction, simplification, and extension. Whether that pattern spreads is an open question worth following.

**Field note / symbiosis:** different participants can contribute different strengths to a shared result. The successful unit may be the partnership, and its dependencies should remain visible.

title: October 21
subtitle: The nursery problem
text:
# October 21

  Human expertise develops through practice, feedback and learning to recognize mistakes. AI can help people complete work, but that does not establish that they acquired the underlying judgment. The question is which kinds of assistance support learning and which bypass useful practice.]

## The nursery problem

 learning]

 learning-nursery:120]

The colony is eating better than ever. The young have stopped learning how to forage. These statements could both be true. That is the uncomfortable possibility raised by Dylan Davis's video about AI and expertise, and by the fuller passage supplied for this workshop. [47]

**Nature sometimes makes room for a lesson.** Wild meerkats give pups opportunities to handle prey. In another study, an experienced ant guided a follower toward food, with signals between them regulating the journey. [52], [53] Feeding another animal and helping it acquire a skill are different achievements. Our workplace analogy begins with that distinction.

If the Relay Octopus sorts every document and drafts every answer, the office may become wonderfully productive. But where does a newcomer learn which detail is suspicious, why an argument fails, or when a polished answer misses the point? The danger we want to investigate is a **bottleneck in the supply of new experts**. It could remain hidden while experienced people still do the checking.

**There is evidence for the concern, and for alternatives.** A school mathematics experiment found that unrestricted AI help improved assisted practice but weakened later unaided performance; a teaching-oriented version largely avoided that loss. A separate programming experiment also found weaker learning with AI help on average. [44], [45] Yet a study of customer-support workers found especially useful gains for less experienced staff, with evidence consistent with learning. [46]

The practical distinction is between help that **supports learning** and help that **bypasses learning**. The research does not establish that every routine task is educational, or that every automated task removes a necessary lesson.

### Field question / Is the nursery still working?

Follow a newcomer through a real task, feedback, and a later attempt on a fresh example. Can they explain a decision, recognize an error, or work through the problem when the assistant is absent? Record improvement separately from the amount of work completed.

This is about learning within a lifetime and knowledge passed between people. It is not evidence of genetic change. The meerkats and ants give us a memorable comparison, not a biological verdict on office life.

title: The borrowed metabolism
subtitle: When a helpful neighbour becomes essential
text:
# The borrowed metabolism

  AI dependence arises when people or organizations rely on an outside system for an important function. Delegation can improve efficiency, while making interruption or loss of access more costly. Dependence and skill loss are different questions and should be tested separately.]

## When a helpful neighbour becomes essential

A microbe does not receive a medal for making everything itself. In the right surroundings, depending on a neighbour can pay.

The **Black Queen hypothesis** describes how microbes may lose costly functions when neighbouring organisms supply their benefits. Separate experiments with engineered bacteria found that partners exchanging essential nutrients could gain a growth advantage over self-sufficient cells under the tested conditions. [54], [55] Dependence can accompany success. The price is that the missing function must still be supplied somewhere.

 borrowed-metabolism:166]

Our AI analogy is an organization that stops maintaining a capability because an assistant reliably supplies it. That might be sensible specialization. It might also leave the organization unable to recognize a bad result or cope when access changes. **Which outcome occurs is a question for observation.**

The analogy has a boundary: genes lost across microbial generations are different from human skills that are never acquired, become rusty, or are deliberately left to a tool. People can retrain and institutions can redesign work. Calling a skill "vestigial" would describe our metaphor, not establish a biological process.

**The human side has its own research history.** Bainbridge's 1983 analysis warned that automation could rely on experienced operators' knowledge while reducing opportunities to acquire or maintain it. Later AI research found that requiring people to think through a decision could reduce excessive reliance on incorrect advice, though it did not eliminate the problem. [56], [57]

The Relay Octopus's cord now carries a second question. We already ask what the AI depends on. We should also ask **what its users have come to depend on it for**. A partnership can be highly capable while one partner loses options.

title: Keeping claws in reserve
subtitle: A loss-of-function ledger for the human habitat
text:
# Keeping claws in reserve

  Delegating work to AI changes which skills people exercise. A delegated skill may remain available, weaken through disuse or be replaced by another method. The practical question is whether people can still judge the output and recover when the assistant is unavailable.]

## A loss-of-function ledger for the human habitat

 learning]

 claws-in-reserve:60]

Our gain-of-function pages follow what AI acquires. Alongside them, we can follow what people stop doing, what they still understand, and what they may need to recover. Delegation is not automatically a loss: the ability may remain intact, or a better way of working may replace it.

**Judgment needs practice too.** Asking someone to approve an answer is not proof that they can assess it. The learning and automation studies give us reasons to test that capacity, rather than assume a human signature supplies it. [44], [45], [56], [57] Nor do they show that beginners and experienced experts suddenly start from the same position.

For each workplace encounter, this proposed ledger would distinguish three choices. They are editorial questions, not a prescription to preserve every old skill.

| Treatment of a skill | Why keep or release it? | What could we observe? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keep in regular use | Needed to understand the task, detect consequential errors, or choose worthwhile goals. | Explain a decision; check an unfamiliar example with planted mistakes. |
| Rehearse as a reserve | Needed occasionally when a system fails or conditions change. | Try a bounded exercise without the usual assistant; record help and recovery time. |
| Delegate with a fallback | Keeping full proficiency may cost more than it contributes in this setting. | Document the alternative person, tool or procedure, and test whether it works. |

**Proposed encounter: two drafts and a diagnosis.** On a safe practice task, have a learner attempt an answer before seeing AI's version. Compare both with an independently checked reference. A mentor explains the differences; the learner then tries a fresh problem. We would report accuracy, understanding and time separately. This exercise is a design to test, not a proven training recipe.

**A new survival question:** does the partnership replenish the expertise it needs? A department can finish more work this quarter while its next generation learns less. It can also use AI to teach better. Our report should look for either outcome, and revisit the balance whenever the tools or the work change.

The future need not be a ladder on which humans endlessly retreat toward "strategy." Checking, choosing goals and teaching can also change. The interesting story is which useful abilities persist, where they reside, and who can still exercise them.

title: The shrinking habitat
subtitle: Homo sapiens laborans / the working human
text:
# The shrinking habitat

  AI can substitute for some human tasks and complement others. Its effects on paid work depend on employers' decisions, changing demand, access and training as well as workers' choices. The working-human feature examines both displacement and useful human-AI partnerships.]

## Homo sapiens laborans / the working human

 employment]

Meet **Homo sapiens laborans**: familiar face, useful hands, and a livelihood that depends on finding work worth doing. Laborans is a playful field-guide name for the working human, not a scientific subspecies. The habitat is the world of paid tasks, employers, customers and opportunities.

 laborans-two-arrangements:210]

### Two arrangements, one human

**Left / Stepping back.** The person hands over the work and withdraws from its decisions. The Octopus occupies the bench; the notebook stays closed. This imagined scene asks what happens when delegation includes surrendering the ability to judge what comes back.

**Right / Working in partnership.** The same person puts the Octopus's capabilities to use, checks the result and chooses the next step. The tools extend the worker's reach while the worker remains involved. Whether this brings lasting advantage needs evidence.

These are possible working arrangements, not two kinds of human. A person can move between them. Delegation can also be a sensible way to free time for other work. Job loss may follow decisions made elsewhere, even when someone has adapted well.

**Where the metaphor bends:** workers can lose demand for their skills without losing the skills themselves. Their choices matter, alongside access to tools, training, bargaining power and employers' decisions. A shrinking niche is no verdict on a person's worth.

title: A partnership worth keeping
subtitle: What does the human actually gain?
text:
# A partnership worth keeping

  Human-AI complementarity means that people and AI contribute different useful abilities to a shared task. Better combined output does not tell us who receives the gains or bears the costs. A worthwhile partnership also needs attention to pay, control, learning and dependence.]

## What does the human actually gain?

 workplace-gains]

A good neighbour can make a larger harvest possible. The next question is who gets the harvest, and what the arrangement costs.

A workplace study found that AI assistance improved customer-support performance, with differing gains across workers. A separate research synthesis found that combining people and AI did not reliably outperform the better of either alone. Useful assistance and a superior partnership are different achievements. [46], [78]

| Partnership check | What would count as an advantage? |
| --- | --- |
| **Purpose and control** | The person can choose useful goals, change course and challenge an unsuitable result. |
| **Quality and effort** | Better usable work, or less human effort for comparable quality, including checking and corrections. |
| **Who receives the gains?** | More income, time, security or worthwhile responsibility for the worker; record employer and supplier gains separately. |
| **Learning and judgment** | The person can explain important decisions and assess unfamiliar results. More output alone does not establish learning. |
| **Room to move** | A workable alternative if access, price or conditions change; record the costs of switching and recovery. |

**Symbiosis, with the terms visible.** The person supplies goals, context and checks; the system supplies useful capabilities. This is a comparison of functions, not a claim that AI has biological needs or interests. Correcting an answer does not automatically retrain the underlying model.

**The checking burden matters.** Research on overreliance suggests that encouraging deliberate thought can improve decisions, with trade-offs in effort and experience. A human signature is not sufficient evidence of supervision. [57]

**Status:** these are proposed reporting questions, not a validated score or a guarantee of employment. Follow a particular person, task and workplace over time; record benefits, dependency and setbacks together.

title: The employment field notebook
subtitle: Five tracks through a changing habitat
text:
# The employment field notebook

  A job contains multiple tasks. Automating some tasks can change the work without eliminating the whole job, while changes in demand can affect hiring, pay and new roles. These outcomes require separate measures rather than a single total of jobs supposedly lost to AI.]

## Five tracks through a changing habitat

 employment]

In Connell's classic barnacle experiments, competition restricted where a species could live. That supplies an image for a narrowing niche. Labor economics supplies a separate explanation: automation can displace human tasks while new tasks create demand for workers. Neither guarantees that displaced people receive the new opportunities. [76], [77]

| Track to follow | What the record must distinguish |
| --- | --- |
| **Lost ground** | Actual dismissals or reduced hours; the affected work, event date and evidence for AI's contribution. |
| **Empty nesting sites** | Fewer entry roles or hires, separate from layoffs. What becomes of the route into expertise? |
| **Changed feeding grounds** | Tasks and pay changing within jobs that still exist; record who gains and who loses. |
| **Working partnerships** | A documented benefit from AI use, including quality, full human effort and the worker's share of the gain. |
| **New niches and migration** | New work and movement into it; skills, location, transition time and access for displaced workers. |

### Q4 case files / first evidence

**Pressure on the nursery:** an October 21 payroll release records weaker employment in highly exposed occupations, especially among young adults. It does not identify the cause of every departure. [79], [80]

**A habitat redesigned:** Barclays announces expected workforce reductions on October 22; the union disputes the approach. Follow implementation and worker outcomes next. [82], [83]

**An advantage borrowed:** October research publications examine assisted task performance and what people understand without the tool. Career benefits remain a separate question. [84], [85]

**Evidence rule:** record event and publication dates separately; compare with the wider sector and check alternative explanations. AI capability, employer attribution and demonstrated job loss are different evidence. General conclusions need independent sources, with academic research explaining the mechanisms.

**Reporting status / October 28:** the following dated pages begin the record. A verified total of Q4 AI-caused job losses, sustained worker benefits and routes into replacement jobs remain open. Keep these outcomes separate; no survival score is assigned.

title: October 21 / employment
subtitle: Fewer footholds for the young
text:
# October 21 / employment

  Early-career employment is one place to look for changes in entry into paid work. Comparing younger workers across occupations with different AI exposure can identify an emerging pattern. The comparison remains an employment indicator, not a direct count of dismissals caused by AI.]

## Fewer footholds for the young

 employment]

A nursery can become harder to enter while the adults remain busy. For Homo sapiens laborans, the first sign of pressure may be a narrower path into paid work.

ADP and Stanford's October release records a contrast: employment in highly AI-exposed occupations fell while the least-exposed group grew. The gap was larger among workers aged 22-25. **These are September-to-September changes released during Q4, not jobs lost during October.** [79]

 employment_snapshot]

**Read the tracks carefully.** Exposure describes tasks an AI might affect; it does not establish that an employer used AI. Employment counts reflect hiring and departures together. This chart cannot tell how much of the change came from layoffs, reduced recruitment or other economic forces. [79], [80]

### A different pool, a different current

In an October 6 research dispatch, Humlum and Vestergaard revisited surveys of **25,000 Danish workers in 11 occupations**, linked to records through December 2024. They found no detectable average effect on earnings or hours, despite changes in tasks. This is an October discussion of earlier research, with an earlier observation window. [81]

**The insight:** a changing task, a shrinking occupation and a lost job are three different sightings. The U.S. payroll pattern deserves attention; the Danish comparison explains why exposure alone cannot identify AI's contribution. Different places, periods and questions can yield different answers.

title: October 22 / employment
subtitle: A habitat redesigned from above
text:
# October 22 / employment

  Employers can combine AI adoption with other changes intended to reduce costs or reorganize work. A workforce announcement describes a plan; completed job losses and their causes require further evidence. This distinction matters when evaluating claims that AI is replacing workers.]

## A habitat redesigned from above

 barclays]

 habitat-engineers:105]

The beaver moves a branch; the current changes for everyone downstream. At work, the equivalent may be a decision made several floors above the people who must adapt.

Barclays' October 22 results presentation set out an **expected reduction of about 5,000 full-time employees**, affecting roughly **5% of its workforce**, from structural cost actions taken in 2026. The bank linked its efficiency plans to organizational simplification and technology change, including AI. Consultation requirements apply. [82]

| The number on the riverbank | What it actually means |
| --- | --- |
| **About 5,000** | Expected reduction associated with the year's cost actions. It is not a count of completed Q4 dismissals. |
| **About 5%** | Approximate share of Barclays employees affected, according to the bank. It is not a percentage of jobs across banking. |
| **AI's contribution** | Not separately quantified. The announcement combines AI with other organizational and technology changes. |

Unite's same-day response challenged the company's AI rationale and called for skills investment, worker involvement and a share of efficiency gains. That is the union's position, not an independent estimate of how many jobs AI caused to disappear. [83]

**Partnership at one level can coexist with pressure at another.** A person might become more capable with AI while an employer redesigns the work around fewer positions. Automation research explains why task gains and labor demand need separate accounting. The announcement supplies a case to follow, not proof of a universal outcome. [77], [82]

**The next sightings:** completed departures, redeployment, changed hiring and the work that remains. None establishes that displaced workers simply chose to let AI take their habitat.

title: October 22
subtitle: The growing appetite for AI
text:
# October 22

  Demand for AI has several signs: current use, intended future use, willingness to pay and investment in capacity. These measures describe different decisions. Business surveys help establish how widely AI is used without proving that every user pays or that every use is productive.]

## The growing appetite for AI

 adoption]

 crowded-watering-hole:168]

The watering hole is busy. Some visitors take a cautious sip; others arrive with buckets. A few are already proposing a larger watering hole.

The Census Bureau's October 22 release provides a timely sighting: **24.6% of U.S. businesses with employees, excluding agriculture, report recent AI use in a business function; 28.6% expect to use it within six months.** These estimates measure use and expectations, not paying customers or next spring's outcome. [70]

 demand_snapshot]

**The appetite is broad, but uneven.** Two research teams help explain the picture. A Census study finds that adoption often reaches only a few business functions. A separate survey of workers finds AI spread across many occupations, while remaining less common within particular tasks. A creature can enter many habitats without taking over every activity inside them. [71], [72]

This substantial foothold leaves room for further adoption. It does not establish equal intensity of use or provider profit. These American survey findings are not worldwide market shares.

title: What keeps the creatures coming?
subtitle: Four signs of demand, four different stories
text:
# What keeps the creatures coming?

  Interest in AI becomes sustained demand when people repeatedly find it useful. Repeated use, paid renewal and a supplier's investment are different signals. Keeping them separate helps distinguish a lasting need from experimentation or a bet on future growth.]

## Four signs of demand, four different stories

 workplace-gains]

 office-reef:100]

Eight arms make an impression. Customers care whether the Relay Octopus finishes the job, and how much help it needs.

Research offers reasons for continued demand. One workplace study finds gains from AI assistance in customer support. Survey research finds workers using it across many kinds of tasks. Useful assistance can create reasons to return, even before an AI can perform an entire job. These findings come from different settings; neither guarantees a benefit in every workplace. [46], [72]

| Sign of demand | What it reveals and leaves open |
| --- | --- |
| **Interest and trials** | People are curious or willing to experiment. A trial can end without a useful habit. |
| **Repeated use** | AI has found a recurring role. Free or bundled use may still reveal little about willingness to pay. |
| **Paid renewals and spending** | Customers continue buying at the offered price. Provider profit still depends on the cost of serving them. |
| **New computing capacity** | Suppliers are preparing for demand. Building capacity is a bet on future customers, not proof they have arrived. |

**Adoption has an apprenticeship.** Research on major technologies explains why benefits can require complementary investment in skills and organization. The AI surveys likewise show that the depth of use matters. Buying an assistant and learning how to work with it are separate achievements. [71]-[73]

Lower costs, easier access and more reliable results could bring additional tasks within reach. The counter-pressure is equally ordinary: checking mistakes, reorganizing work and training people can consume the apparent saving. The cost of the whole meal includes the time spent picking out the bones. [40], [56]

title: When the feeding grounds fill
subtitle: The demand for AI creates demands of its own
text:
# When the feeding grounds fill

  Meeting AI demand requires computing capacity, electricity, investment and human work. A shortage in one can raise costs or limit access even if models improve. Demand and available supply must therefore be examined together, using a separate measure for each resource.]

## The demand for AI creates demands of its own

 energy]

 habitat-engineers:125]

People want useful results. Delivering those results calls on electricity, equipment, money and human attention. These are connected appetites, but counting one does not measure all the others.

**The physical appetite is already substantial.** The International Energy Agency estimates that data centres worldwide used about **485 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2025**, and projects roughly **950 in 2030** in its central outlook. The latter is a projection. Both figures cover all data centres, including non-AI activity; they are not measurements of AI alone. [74]

A cheaper mouthful need not mean a smaller total meal. If serving each task takes less energy but many more tasks are attempted, total use can still rise. Research measuring AI's operating energy finds large differences across tasks and models; the energy outlook also considers changing efficiency and workload. There is no single enduring electricity price tag for an "AI question." [74], [75]

**The bottleneck can move.** More chips do not immediately provide a power connection, a dependable answer or a colleague who knows when to question it. Energy analysis and research on organizational investment describe different constraints on expansion. Removing one can make another more noticeable. [73], [74]

The ecological analogy is **carrying capacity**: the activity that available resources can support. For AI, infrastructure, efficiency, prices and human choices can change the limits. The comparison does not imply a fixed number of AI creatures that the planet can hold.

**The implications reach outside the enclosure.** Growing demand could widen access to useful assistance while increasing pressure on local electricity systems. Scarcity could favor well-funded providers; it could also reward economical specialists. These are possibilities to investigate. A full order book alone does not show which species will thrive, who will benefit, or who will bear the costs.

title: Three seasons ahead
subtitle: Possible paths through 2027, with an eye on 2030
text:
# Three seasons ahead

  Future AI demand depends on adoption, useful results, costs and the capacity to serve users. A scenario describes what could happen under stated conditions; it is not an observed trend or a probability estimate. Different sectors can follow different paths at the same time.]

## Possible paths through 2027, with an eye on 2030

 changing-weather:90]

The evidence leaves room for substantial further adoption. The speed, depth and commercial return remain open. These are conditional scenarios informed by adoption, organizational and energy research; no probabilities are assigned. Different sectors could experience them at the same time. [70]-[75]

| Possible season | What would make it visible? | What could follow? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **The bloom spreads** | Customers renew; useful tasks multiply; benefits survive careful comparison. | AI becomes ordinary infrastructure. More niches open for specialists, and affordable access matters increasingly. |
| **The crowded waterhole** | Demand outpaces power, equipment, reliable service or staff able to integrate it. | Delays and selective access favor those with resources. Efficiency and simpler systems become more valuable. |
| **The thinning season** | Trials fail to renew; buyers cut spending that does not justify its total cost. | Products consolidate or disappear. Useful niches can persist even while some suppliers struggle. |

**Jobs are part of the habitat.** More AI use can change which tasks people perform and which skills they need. Usage counts alone do not reveal net jobs gained or lost. The nursery must also keep functioning: does the partnership develop the expertise it depends on? [44], [46], [72]

### Recurring watch / Is the new habitat sustainable?

At year-end, look for paid renewals, useful work per customer, total cost including human review, access delays, and evidence of learning or lost capability. Record whose measure it is and what it leaves out. Each measure answers a different question; no single score captures the health of the whole habitat.

**The question for the next season:** will more visitors arrive, will returning users find more useful tasks, and will enough keep paying to sustain the services they choose?

The central survival question is whether a service keeps earning its place when the novelty wears off. Expanding demand can support many creatures. It does not make every creature fit for its niche.

title: October 25-26
subtitle: Who gets to inspect the web?
text:
# October 25-26

  Access to AI includes access to systems, their outputs and the material needed to check claims about them. Publication policies and operating prices affect who can participate. These access decisions can change how widely a capability benefits researchers or other users.]

## Who gets to inspect the web?

 prices]

 access-to-web:68]

The mathematical dispute continued. On October 25, the independent advisory group argued against companies choosing particular mathematicians to lead the understanding and presentation of their output. It raised concerns about unequal access, influence over research priorities, and the use of scholars' reputations. On October 26, it called for prompt public release of material behind announced claims in mathematical physics. These are the group's stated concerns and recommendations. [17]

The future-facing question is plain: if powerful AI systems produce important ideas, who gets to examine them, develop them, and decide what they mean? Access to the new animal can become power over the surrounding habitat.

### October 26 / Another arrival at the feeding ground

OpenAI recorded GPT-6.1 Terra's rollout. Its published prices join a landscape in which the cost of using an AI can shape where it is useful. [7]

 prices]

The billing unit, a token, is a small piece of text. Different systems may need different amounts of text and different numbers of attempts to finish the same job. The chart compares unit prices only; it does not establish which system is the better bargain.

**The useful eventual measure:** how much money, time, and checking were needed to obtain a result someone could actually use?

title: October 26 / research
subtitle: The borrowed exoskeleton
text:
# October 26 / research

  Assisted performance is what someone can accomplish while using AI. Retained learning is what they understand or can do afterward, including without assistance. An experiment must test these separately before better immediate output can be treated as evidence of lasting skill.]

## The borrowed exoskeleton

 task-expansion]

 learning-nursery:80]

A borrowed shell can widen the territory a creature can enter. What happens when the shell comes off? October's research publications give that question a practical human counterpart.

A study published in **Nature Human Behaviour on October 26** tested **487 management consultants** on unfamiliar data-science work. AI access and training improved performance on three tasks, but did not bring the consultants to the expert benchmark. The researchers found no evidence of better answers to technical questions afterwards without AI. This is a new journal publication of work that had circulated earlier. [84]

### Another route beyond familiar territory

An independent **October 2026 working paper** studied **673 final-year IT apprentices at 12 German schools**. AI access raised the share of available marks earned by **26 and 31 percentage points** on two tasks beyond their formal curriculum. It found no reduction in immediate task comprehension. The experiment ran from October 2025 to January 2026; the paper is not yet peer reviewed. [85]

| What can change? | What these studies leave open |
| --- | --- |
| **Reach with assistance** | Better performance on unfamiliar tasks is possible. That does not establish professional expertise. |
| **Understanding without it** | Results differ across tasks and tests. Immediate comprehension is not the same as durable learning. |
| **A worker's prospects** | Neither study measures jobs saved, lasting pay gains or long-term career security. |

**The insight:** ask whether the partnership extends a person's reach, develops their own abilities, or does both. The studies support assisted performance in different settings; they do not settle long-term learning in either direction. For laborans, the most useful field test has two parts: work with the partner, then check what can still be explained and done alone. [84], [85]

title: Mathematics after the rain
subtitle: The upheaval is bigger than a scoreboard
text:
# Mathematics after the rain

  AI-assisted mathematical discovery involves proposing results, checking correctness, explaining arguments and deciding what to build on. Success at one stage does not settle the others. The disruption concerns how researchers manage all of these activities as machine-generated work enters their field.]

## The upheaval is bigger than a scoreboard

 math-catalogue]

The mathematical story is already a major disruption in the way a research community receives work and debates its future. The public release, organized opposition, new funding, and human follow-up are observable events. The final value of each proposed result still has to be assessed separately.

 understanding-the-web:166]

**Checking is not the whole of understanding.** A proof-checking program can verify that a precisely expressed argument follows its rules and assumptions. People still need to establish that the formal statement matches the intended question, place the result in existing knowledge, and explain why it matters. Avigad's work on proof and understanding examines this wider mathematical activity; the advisory group's September guidance brings it into the present dispute. [50], [12]

**The question-setter may become more powerful.** A future rich in answers could place greater importance on which questions receive attention. This possibility concerns mathematicians, but it also matters wherever AI helps choose research directions.

**There is a research history beneath the headlines.** AlphaGeometry combined learned suggestions with a rule-based geometry engine in a 2024 Nature paper. [49] October's human follow-up reports a different partnership: people reworking AI-produced arguments. [16] Together they show more than one way machines can contribute to mathematical work; neither certifies every claim in the new collection.

**New niches may emerge.** Explaining difficult AI output, testing claims, designing questions, and connecting discoveries to applications are plausible roles. We should watch whether these become durable opportunities. It would be premature to publish an extinction notice for mathematicians.

The Proofweaver gives us a recurring image for this story. We will watch its webs, the tools used to inspect them, and the people deciding which paths through the forest are worth exploring.

title: The Habitat Engineers
subtitle: When the newcomer rearranges the river
text:
# The Habitat Engineers

  AI's development is shaped by institutions as well as models. Companies, funders, governments and professional communities influence access, standards, costs and research priorities. Their decisions change the conditions under which different AI systems can be developed and used.]

## When the newcomer rearranges the river

 funding]

A beaver's dam changes the conditions in which other creatures live. Ecologists call organisms that physically reshape habitats **ecosystem engineers**. Related work on **niche construction** examines how organisms alter conditions that affect selection. The ideas overlap, but they are not identical. [58], [59]

For this magazine, the question is what people rebuild around AI. Do they change the forms, the review process, the training route, or even the questions worth asking? The mathematics dispute and the nursery problem give us places to investigate. A changed habitat may create opportunities for some inhabitants and difficulties for others.

 habitat-engineers:166]

### Reserved case / follow one changed practice

Choose a research group, classroom or workplace with documented practices before and after adoption. Record who changed what, why they changed it, and whose work became easier or harder. Keep other explanations in view. A new rule appearing after an AI launch does not establish that the launch caused it.

**Academic starting points:** the existing studies of assisted learning and workplace assistance show different outcomes in different settings. They guide our questions about design and use; they do not yet demonstrate the broader institutional changes proposed here. [44], [46]

**Reporting status:** the case and its documented before-and-after comparison remain open for further reporting. There is no measured claim here that AI has redesigned an entire profession.

**Where the metaphor bends:** people and institutions make these changes. The metaphor does not give software an independent intention to build a habitat.

title: The Naturalist Was Wrong
subtitle: October's endangered expectations
text:
# The Naturalist Was Wrong

  An AI result challenges an expectation only if we know what was expected and what the new evidence establishes. Dated predictions, unstated assumptions and claims of surprise need different treatment. Comparing them carefully shows which beliefs actually need revision.]

## October's endangered expectations

 naturalist-surprised:166]

The naturalist arrives carrying a confident field guide. By lunchtime, the bird has borrowed a screwdriver, the octopus has hired assistants, and the spider has submitted a paper. The field guide requires an appendix.

A supplied transcript tells a lively story: predictions of a ceiling for large language models gave way to new routes to improvement. [26] It invites us to revisit expectations. But it also bundles the skeptics together, bundles the optimists together, and awards the jungle to the winner.

### Past / Keep the original prediction in view

A warning that training data may become scarce is different from a prediction that all AI progress will stop. Epoch's 2024 study projected possible full use of public human text between 2026 and 2032 under specified trends; it also considered other sources of progress. October's advances do not, by themselves, refute that forecast. [32]

Nor was everybody surprised. In a February 2026 interview, Dario Amodei described the broad progress of models as roughly consistent with his earlier expectations, while acknowledging unevenness. That is one person's account, but enough to complicate the transcript's opening chorus. [33]

title: Expectations under pressure
subtitle: What October is making us reconsider
text:
# Expectations under pressure

  Assumptions about AI often connect one observation to a wider conclusion: a higher score to general reliability, or lower prices to better value. Those connections need evidence of their own. Examining them makes the difference between a measured result and an expectation explicit.]

## What October is making us reconsider

 naturalist-surprised:100]


These are assumptions for the reader to examine, not attributed quotations or a survey of what researchers believed.

| Expectation under pressure | October encounter | Our provisional reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AI can imitate mathematical prose, but contribute nothing useful to research. | A human team reports a stronger, shorter argument after examining AI-produced work, October 16. [16] | A specific challenge to the blanket dismissal; each result still needs assessment. |
| Producing a correct answer finishes the important work. | The October 6 release brings questions of understanding and access, followed by organized support. [13], [15] | The surrounding community has work the scoreboard misses. |
| A more capable assistant must have acquired a bigger brain. | October's workplace offerings add tools, connections and permissions. [5]-[6] | Examine the whole system before assigning the gain to its model. |

**The surprise is ecological.** A new ability can move the shortage elsewhere: from proposing answers to checking them, from finding information to deciding what deserves attention. Our interpretation is that success changes the habitat as well as the creature.

To declare a failed forecast, preserve its author, date, conditions and contrary evidence. Until then, call it an **expectation under pressure**.

title: The wall grew doors
subtitle: More than one route to a better creature
text:
# The wall grew doors

  AI capability can improve through changes to training, additional computation while answering, external tools or coordination among systems. An improvement in the complete working system need not come from a larger or newly trained model. The source of a gain matters when judging its limits.]

## More than one route to a better creature

 agent-teams]
